extracted.intended_audience: small businesses (SBCs) applying for SBIR/STTR Phase II funding; SBIR/STTR awardees and program managers
extracted.subtask_description: Explains the different Phase II funding variations and program rules (Direct to Phase II, sequential Phase IIs, Phase IIA/IIB, Cross-Agency/Program, Open Phase II, award caps, and special bridge awards) and how they vary by Federal Agency. Provides practical guidance on eligibility, award amounts, and whom to contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct to Phase II (DP2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct to Phase II enabled an Agency to issue a Phase II award to a small business concern that did not receive a Phase I award for research and development for the same project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DP2 was a pilot from the SBIR/STTR Reauthorization Act of 2011 for firms that had completed Phase I milestones using non-SBIR funds. DARPA first implemented DP2, followed by NIH and the Air Force. The pilot expired but was reauthorized (via the National Defense Authorization Act, Aug 2018) and was anticipated to be available again (e.g., FY19). Availability and implementation vary by Agency—contact the SBIR/STTR program manager for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential Phase II awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows a Phase II awardee to receive one additional sequential Phase II award to continue the work of an initial Phase II award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The additional sequential Phase II has the same guideline amounts and limits as the initial Phase II (guideline amount of $1 million and a limit of $1.5 million). SBCs interested in sequential Phase IIs should discuss the application process with their technical monitor or the Agency's SBIR/STTR program manager. Agencies differ in implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase IIA vs Phase IIB distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Agencies use Phase IIA and Phase IIB labels for additional funding opportunities, with meanings that vary across Agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (DOE): Phase IIA allows a Phase II grantee to complete R&D associated with the initial prototype/product/process development; DOE Phase IIB provides additional support for a new R&D task that extends beyond the original Phase II scope. Not every Agency offers these awards and internal guidelines vary—consult your Agency's guidance or program manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCI SBIR Phase IIB Bridge Award
rubrics_metrics.description: A funding opportunity to support the next stage of development for NIH-funded SBIR Phase II projects in cancer areas, intended to bridge the 'Valley of Death' to commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bridge Award incentivizes partnerships between NIH SBIR Phase II awardees and third-party investors or strategic partners. It targets therapeutics, imaging technologies, interventional devices, diagnostics, and prognostics. SBIR and STTR Phase II awardees from other Federal Agencies are welcome to apply. The program is explicitly designed to address the funding gap between Phase II and later-stage financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-program awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanism enabling switching between SBIR and STTR across phases (e.g., a Phase I STTR award winner may receive a Phase II SBIR award or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-program flexibility allows projects to move between SBIR and STTR programs when that better fits the commercialization path. Availability and procedures vary by Agency—consult the SBIR program manager responsible for your Phase I award to explore options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Agency awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows any Agency to fund a Phase II initiative that was initially funded by another Agency in Phase I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-Agency awards are useful when the original Phase I funding Agency lacks funds for Phase II; they can bring new technologies into an Agency's portfolio that meet urgent needs. Coordination with the Phase I program manager is recommended to pursue this option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Phase II competition (DoD change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy change enabling all DoD Phase I awardees to submit Phase II proposals without invitation; mechanism varies by Service/Component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously, DoD Phase I awardees were only invited to submit Phase II proposals if a Service/Component expressed interest. Now all DoD Phase I awardees may submit Phase II proposals, but submission mechanisms differ by Service/Component. Civilian Agencies have generally allowed Phase I awardees to apply for Phase II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award caps and guideline amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Across Agencies, ceilings/caps may be placed on SBIR/STTR awards; an Agency may cap awards at 150% of the base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 150% cap example: $225,000 for Phase I and $1.5 million for Phase II. Agencies have discretion to set award sizes and may offer smaller awards to increase the number of awards. SBA-approved topics list permits budgets to exceed hard caps for listed topics, and HHS has topic waivers for hard caps. Always check Agency-specific guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget source and Agency discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding for additional Phase II opportunities comes from the same pool of SBIR/STTR funds; Agencies decide size/number of Phase I/Phase II/sequential awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller Agencies with smaller budgets are less likely to fund additional Phase II opportunities, though they may use Cross-Agency awards to bring in technologies. Larger Agencies tend to implement more of these additional opportunities. Review Agency allocations and discuss with program managers to understand realistic prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and limited availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition for additional Phase II opportunities is significant because the number of these awards is limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should carefully review Agency guidelines and discuss the wisdom of pursuing these opportunities with their technical monitor or SBIR/STTR program manager. Expect high competition and plan commercialization/funding strategies accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency variation and need to consult program staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant Agency differences mean not all Phase II variations apply to every situation; guidelines often vary within Agencies and between entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, contact the SBIR or STTR program manager for the Agency of interest or your technical monitor. Agency-specific guidance determines eligibility, application process, caps, topic waivers, and mechanisms for Direct to Phase II, sequential awards, cross-program/agency awards, and open competitions.
